## Body heating, top cooling and bottom heating (`body-heat`, `top-cool`, `bot-heat`) {#sec-ch09-heating}

### Summary

These three modules are prescribed heat sources for idealised convection. They touch only the total energy, so
they change the temperature and, through it, the pressure; mass and momentum are untouched. `body-heat` is a
volumetric rate; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` stand for a radiative or surface flux at the top or bottom of the
domain, applied only by the block that owns that physical $x_1$ boundary.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** `body-heat` heats every interior cell whose pressure lies in a band at a fixed rate of temperature
change at constant volume; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` remove or add a fixed energy flux, spread evenly over the top
or bottom `depth` cells; @eq-ch09-heating-body and @eq-ch09-heating-flux.

**Data.** In: density, pressure, $c_v$, heat rate or boundary flux and depth; out: the stage energy increment.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, in the forcing loop; `top-cool` and `bot-heat` only on the block that owns the
physical $x_1$ boundary.

**Activation.** `forcing/body-heat: {dTdt, pmin, pmax}`, defaults 0, 0, 1 [$\mathrm{K\,s^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{Pa}$,
$\mathrm{Pa}$]; `top-cool: {flux, depth}`, `flux` $\le0$, defaults 0 and 1; `bot-heat: {flux, depth}`, `flux`
$\ge0$, defaults 0 and 1 [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, cells]. Each off unless its key is present.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact pointwise sources; the column receives exactly $F$ only on uniform cells and not on
curved grids; the default `pmax` of 1 $\mathrm{Pa}$ heats almost nothing.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test assertions are listed below; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

**Data details.** In: the interior density $\rho$, pressure $p$ [$\mathrm{Pa}$] and mixture $c_v$ (`body-heat`); the
flux $F$ [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$], `depth` and the $x_1$ width `dz` of the boundary cell (`top-cool`, `bot-heat`); $\Delta t$.
Out: the energy row of the increment, per unit volume [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$]. Check cases: $F=-30$
$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ with `depth` 4 on uniform cells and on cells growing upward by 10 %.

**Evidence details.** Tests: heating only inside the pressure band with the mixture $c_v$,
{{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.body_heat_uses_pressure_mask_and_mixture_cv >}}; linearity of the boundary
fluxes in $\Delta t$, {{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.boundary_fluxes_scale_with_timestep >}} (both
`allclose` defaults); these ctests were not run at the pin. No test of the delivered column total. Check:
`python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/heating_check.py`, output `heating_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C3]`, re-run at the pin: all PASS, output identical [^env-heating].

Local symbols (flagged to the editor, ISSUES.md): $\dot T$ [K s$^{-1}$] the heating rate `dTdt`; $p_{\min}$, $p_{\max}$ [Pa]
the pressure band; $F$ [W m$^{-2}$] the boundary flux `flux`; $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ the number of cells `depth` it is spread
over (NOTATION.md does not use a bare $d$); $\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ [m] the $x_1$ width of the boundary cell, `dz`;
$\overline{\Delta x_1}$ [m] the mean $x_1$ width of the $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells; $E_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_iE_iV_i$ [J] the integrated total
energy. $\rho$, $p$, $c_v$, $E$, $\Delta t$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are NOTATION.md's.

The default `pmax` is 1 $\mathrm{Pa}$: a `body-heat` block that does not set `pmin` and `pmax` heats only cells with
$0\le p\le1$ $\mathrm{Pa}$, which in most decks is none.

### Derivation

*Body heating.* At constant volume the internal energy density changes by $\rho c_v\,\mathrm{d}T$, so a heating rate
$\dot T$ adds, in one stage and in every interior cell with $p_{\min}\le p_i\le p_{\max}$,

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\dot T\,\rho_ic_{v,i} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-body}

with $c_v$ the mixture value of the equation of state at the cell's state, in `BodyHeatImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatImpl::forward >}}). For a constant $c_v$ at fixed density this raises
$T$ by exactly $\dot T\Delta t$;[^heat-c3] a $c_v$ that depends on $T$ makes it first order in $\Delta t$.

*Boundary fluxes.* A flux $F$ [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$] spread over the $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells next to the boundary is applied to
each of those cells as a uniform volumetric rate

$$
\Delta E_i = \Delta t\,\frac{F}{\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}\,n_{\mathrm{dep}}} ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-heating-flux}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-heating-flux ch09_dropin_check.py [D2] -->

with $\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ the $x_1$ width of the boundary cell, `dz`, in `TopCoolImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}}) and `BotHeatImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::forward >}}). What the column receives follows in three steps.

1. *Per cell.* Each of the $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells gains @eq-ch09-heating-flux, the same value in every cell.
2. *Per unit horizontal area.* On a Cartesian grid a cell's energy is $E_i\Delta x_{1,i}$ per unit area, so the column
   gains $\sum_i\Delta E_i\,\Delta x_{1,i} = \Delta t\,F\,n_{\mathrm{dep}}\overline{\Delta x_1}/(\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}n_{\mathrm{dep}})
   = \Delta t\,F\,\overline{\Delta x_1}/\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$.
3. *Hence* exactly $F$ per unit time on uniform cells, and $F\,\overline{\Delta x_1}/\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ otherwise: 0.872 for
   cells growing upward by 10 % with $n_{\mathrm{dep}}=4$.[^heat-c12]

*Round-off.* The per-cell value `dt * flux / (dz * depth)` carries three roundings (the two products and the
division), so it is within $3\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2$ relative of $\Delta t\,F/(\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}n_{\mathrm{dep}})$, and the
delivered column energy within the same relative bound (check: at most 0.870 of it). Adding it into the energy
row adds one more rounding of the row's new value, $\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\lvert\Delta E_i^{\mathrm{new}}\rvert$, which is relative to the
whole increment of the cell, not to the heating. On a spherical-polar grid the cell volume is not $\Delta x_1$ times a fixed area, so the
delivered power is not $F$ either; not measured.

*Exact and truncated.* Both sources are exact pointwise for the stage-entry state; nothing is truncated in space.

[^heat-c3]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/heating_check.py`, output `heating_check.out`, line `[C3]`; a numpy port
    of the three `forward` functions at the pin, double precision.
[^heat-c12]: Same command, lines `[C1]` (uniform cells: $-30$ $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$ delivered for $F=-30$, $n_{\mathrm{dep}}=4$) and
    `[C2]` (ratio 0.871713).

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-heating-column shows where each module acts.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-heating-column
#| fig-cap: "Where the three heating modules act in an $x_1$ column bounded by walls (thick black lines). Blue: the top $n_{\\mathrm{dep}}$ cells cooled by top-cool, a flux $F\\le0$ in $\\mathrm{W\\,m^{-2}}$; vermillion: the bottom $n_{\\mathrm{dep}}$ cells heated by bot-heat, $F\\ge0$; orange: the cells inside the pressure band $p_{\\min}\\le p\\le p_{\\max}$ (in $\\mathrm{Pa}$) of body-heat; light blue: untouched cells."
#| fig-alt: "A vertical stack of ten cells with the top three, the bottom two and three middle cells shaded, each labelled with the module and its formula."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_heating_column import make_fig
make_fig()
```

All three are cell sources: no stencil and no ghosts are read. `body-heat` acts on interior cells only.
`top-cool` and `bot-heat` slice only in $x_1$, so they also write the $x_2$, $x_3$ ghost cells of their rows, which
the boundary fill overwrites. They run in every stage, explicit, in the forcing loop (@sec-ch09-framework).

### Code

**A minimal input.** Convection driven from below and cooled from above:

```yaml
forcing:
  bot-heat: {flux: 30., depth: 2}            # W m^-2 >= 0, spread over the 2 bottom cells
  top-cool: {flux: -30., depth: 2}           # W m^-2 <= 0
  body-heat: {dTdt: 1.e-5, pmin: 5.e4, pmax: 1.e5}   # K s^-1 inside 0.5-1 bar; pmax defaults to 1 Pa
```

**What is refused, and why.**

1. *An unknown key* in each block, by `check_keys`.
2. *`pmin` > `pmax`*, with "BodyHeatOptions: pmin must not exceed pmax." ({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp >}}): the band would be empty.
3. *A positive `top-cool` flux*, with "TopCool flux must be negative" ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp >}}; zero is accepted), and a
   negative `bot-heat` flux, with "BotHeat flux must be positive" ({{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp >}}; zero is accepted): each
   module has one direction.
4. *`depth` $\le0$*, with "TopCool depth must be greater than zero" or "BotHeat depth must be greater than zero"
   ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp >}}, {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch09-heating-body and @eq-ch09-heating-flux:**

```cpp
// BodyHeatImpl::forward
auto mask =
    torch::logical_and(pres >= options->pmin(), pres <= options->pmax());
du[IPR].index(interior) += torch::where(mask, dt * options->dTdt() * rho * cv,
                                        torch::zeros_like(pres));
// TopCoolImpl::forward
if (!phydro->pmb->options->is_physical_boundary(0, 0, 1)) return du;
auto dz = pcoord->dx1f[iu];
du[IPR].slice(-1, iu + 1 - options->depth(), iu + 1) +=
    dt * options->flux() / (dz * options->depth());
```

`mask` is $p_{\min}\le p_i\le p_{\max}$ and the `where` line @eq-ch09-heating-body; `dz` is $\Delta x_{1,\mathrm b}$ of the top cell
and the last line @eq-ch09-heating-flux on the top $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells. `BotHeatImpl::forward` is the mirror image with
`narrow(-1, il, depth)` and `dx1f[il]`.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| options, `pmin` $\le$ `pmax` | {{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `BodyHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml` | `body-heat` |
| @eq-ch09-heating-body | {{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatImpl::forward >}} | `BodyHeatImpl::forward` | |
| options, `flux` $\le0$ | {{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `TopCoolOptionsImpl::from_yaml` | `top-cool` |
| @eq-ch09-heating-flux, top | {{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}} | `TopCoolImpl::forward` | |
| options, `flux` $\ge0$ | {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `BotHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml` | `bot-heat` |
| @eq-ch09-heating-flux, bottom | {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::forward >}} | `BotHeatImpl::forward` | |

: Code map of the heating modules. {#tbl-ch09-heating-code}

1. Each `from_yaml` checks its keys and values: `pmin` $\le$ `pmax` for `body-heat`, the sign of `flux` and a
   positive `depth` for the two boundary fluxes
   ({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. `BodyHeatImpl::forward` masks the interior by the pressure band and adds @eq-ch09-heating-body
   ({{< code src/forcing/body_heat.cpp BodyHeatImpl::forward >}}).
3. `TopCoolImpl::forward` and `BotHeatImpl::forward` return at once unless the block's upper or lower $x_1$ face is
   physical, then add @eq-ch09-heating-flux ({{< code src/forcing/top_cool.cpp TopCoolImpl::forward >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/bot_heat.cpp BotHeatImpl::forward >}}).

### Limits

1. **Stretched cells.** @eq-ch09-heating-flux uses the boundary cell's width for all $n_{\mathrm{dep}}$ cells, so the delivered
   power is $F$ only on uniform cells (`[C2]`).
2. **Curved grids.** No correction for the cell volume of spherical-polar or cubed-sphere grids; not measured.
3. **`depth` against the block.** `depth` is checked to be positive but not against the block's $x_1$ cell count;
   the `depth` cells are taken in the block that owns the boundary, and no other block applies the flux, so under
   an $x_1$ split a `depth` that reaches past that block is not continued into the next. A `depth` beyond the interior can select ghost cells with `top-cool`;
   `bot-heat` throws when its `narrow` extends beyond the allocated tensor. Keep `depth` within the interior.
4. **`body-heat` default band** `pmax` = 1 $\mathrm{Pa}$ (above).


[^env-heating]: Recorded run environment: Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.
